The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{2}+x-3)^{′}=2x+1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{2}+{x}_{n}-3}{2{x}_{n}+1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(2{x}_{n}+1)-({x}_{n}^{2}+{x}_{n}-3)}{2{x}_{n}+1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}^{2}+3}{2{x}_{n}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{{x}_{0}^{2}+3}{2{x}_{0}+1} \\  & =\frac{(0.8)^{2}+3}{2(0.8)+1} \\  & =\frac{3.64}{2.6} \\  & =1.4.\end{aligned}
$$
